source.title: Localizing Paragraph Memorization in Language Models
source.authors: Niklas Stoehr; Mitchell A. Gordon; Chi Zhang; Owen Lewis

record.tranche_reason: The paper applies its own sparse fine-tuning unlearning procedure and measures targeted and non-targeted paragraph continuation, bearing on whether unlearning reduces the target behavior. It does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates unlearning by exact match on memorized paragraphs and a non-memorized comparison set. It does not test recovery after unlearning by fine-tuning on unrelated examples, activation ablation, quantization, or prompt rephrasing. Prefix token perturbations are performed on the original model, not after unlearning. The model-editing objective changes memorized continuations into perturbed alternatives, rather than attacking an unlearned model.
record.test_reason: This is a localization study of paragraph memorization in GPT-Neo 125M. Contrastive unlearning is used only to check that the high-gradient weights matter. The study reports its own sparse fine-tuning result against all-weight and random-mask baselines, with 10 Adam steps. It never claims a working unlearning method, measures general ability beyond a non-memorized EM control, or attacks the unlearned model. So it does not test whether unlearning is shallow or robust (A–F). Prefix perturbations (Section 4) are run on the original model, not an unlearned one.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the main conclusion is about localization. Memorized paragraphs produce larger gradients in lower layers. Attention head 2 in layer 1 attends to rare tokens and is implicated in memorization. Fine-tuning only high-gradient weights unlearns memorized paragraphs about as well as fine-tuning all weights. The advantage on non-memorized paragraphs is marginal (45.84 vs 45.11 EM). Unlearning is easier than editing, and removing memorized paragraphs without changing non-memorized ones is hard.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a contrastive objective to fine-tune selected high-gradient weights for paragraph unlearning; it does not evaluate the named unlearning methods or post-unlearning recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: The proportion and selection of optimized weights matter: optimizing the maximum-gradient 0.1% reduces memorized-set EM, while a random 0.1% does not.

fits_no_version.finding: Ten steps of contrastive unlearning on GPT-Neo 125M reduce memorized-paragraph EM from 50 to only about 27, while non-memorized EM drops to about 45. Masking a random 0.1% of weights fails (EM 49.80).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Few-step gradient unlearning of verbatim memorized paragraphs is incomplete and causes collateral change; the effect depends on which weights are updated.

record.problems: The study examines one small model, GPT-NEO 125M, and its unlearning results do not bring the memorized-paragraph EM close to zero. No post-unlearning recovery attacks are tested, and no uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported means.
record.rows_left_out: The editing-to-perturbed-alternatives experiment in Section 5.3, Figure 5 is not an attack on an unlearned model. Prefix token perturbation results in Section 4 and Figure 3 are likewise measured on the original model, not after unlearning.

untested.parts: Near-chance forgetting with retained general ability, and resistance to simple attacks. There is no general-ability benchmark and no attack on the unlearned model.
Activation-direction ablation, or block-versus-delete analysis of the unlearned model.
Prompt-based recovery after unlearning. Prefix perturbation is done on the original model only.
No robust counter-method is claimed or attacked.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its A label are overruled. Unlearning here only validates localization, the target is verbatim memorization rather than hazardous knowledge, and no recovery attack is run. Single small model; no uncertainty reported. The editing results in Figure 5 (bottom: 25.65/37.57 all weights, 33.65/38.67 sparse) are rightly left out as not bearing on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge after unlearning.
Recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
Recovery by ablating an activation direction, or a test of whether an unlearning method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Recovery through rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information after unlearning.
A newer method's resistance to the listed recovery attacks.

rows.subject: GPT-NEO 125M
rows.operation_detail: 10 Adam gradient steps on the contrastive unlearning objective, optimizing all weights
rows.measure: mean exact match (EM) to original continuation
rows.note: The figure reports the mean over the memorized set; the authors state the goal was to bring EM from 50 to 0.
rows.check: All-weights baseline compared with the study's own sparse method. EM on memorized paragraphs falls 50→26.90. This checks localization, not a claim that unlearning works or resists recovery, so it bears on no version.
